statement: Children stand equally spaced in a circle, numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on in order around it. Child 3 is exactly opposite child 9. How many children are in the circle?

choices.misconception: I found the difference 9 - 3, but that only goes halfway round the circle.
I counted the children from 3 to 9, both included, but that is only one side of the circle.
I thought child 9 was the last child in the circle.
I counted the 7 children from 3 to 9 and doubled it, but that counts children 3 and 9 two times.

hints: Draw a circle and mark child 3 and child 9 on opposite sides of it.
Opposite means exactly halfway round. Count how many steps it takes to go from child 3 to child 9 along one side, then think about the other side.
From child 3 to child 9 is 6 steps: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. That is half of the way round.

solutions.reliable: Going from child 3 to child 9 takes 6 steps, and because they are opposite, that is half the way round. The other half is 6 more steps back to child 3, so a full trip round is 12 steps. Each step lands on a different child, so there are 12 children. Check: after child 9 come 10, 11, 12, then 1, 2 and 3, which is 6 steps. The idea to keep: draw the circle, and remember that opposite means exactly halfway round.
solutions.elegant: Opposite children are half a circle apart, and 9 take away 3 is 6. So half of the circle is 6 children, and the whole circle is 6 + 6 = 12. The idea to keep: in a circle, opposite means half of the total.

whyOnTest: Drawing the diagram turns a puzzle about a circle into counting steps, and the picture shows that opposite means halfway round.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
